description:
About this role 
 
 
 What team will you be on? 
 The regional APAC ex-Japan Request for Proposal (RFP) function within APAC Institutional Client Business oversees strategic proposal development and drives coordination across Institutional distribution channels, playing a key role in securing new business. Based in Hong Kong, the team collaborates closely with colleagues across Institutional Client Business, product strategy, and other business functions to provide high-quality, consistent, and cohesive quantitative and qualitative information to prospects and consultants.

 Why is your role important? 
 The RFP Writer (Associate) leads the drafting of detailed proposals for major institutional APAC ex-Japan clients across a diverse range of BlackRock’s products, playing a vital role in winning new business. The role requires a strong understanding of BlackRock’s offerings, strategies, structure, and unique selling points to convey these effectively in RFPs and other new business-related documents to secure assets. The role offers considerable exposure to a wide range of products and key internal clients, particularly in APAC ex-Japan, and the opportunity to build a high profile and develop within the business over the medium term.

 What will you be doing? 
 Managing RFPs within a defined scope, delivering consistent, high-quality, and timely responses in collaboration with key stakeholders on a diverse range of products, including alternatives, equity, fixed income, multi-asset investments, and custom solutions
 Representing the team professionally with colleagues, clients, and stakeholders, making sound decisions within the role’s scope and escalating risks appropriately
 Supporting the training of junior RFP writers in the region through expertise and partnership, while liaising with global peers to maintain consistent global practices
 Partnering with product strategy teams to build growing subject matter expertise in how they invest money on behalf of clients
 Refreshing and improving RFP Q&A database content on an ongoing basis, and playing a key role in its continuous improvement
 Contributing ideas and insights that improve execution, and contributing to team projects, including designing solutions with long-term impact and using AI-enabled tools to streamline work, reduce manual effort, and increase team efficiency
 
 What are we looking for? 
 A degree and 3+ years of financial services experience. Prior experience as a RFP writer is highly preferred
 High standards of excellence, urgency, and accountability, with the ability to prioritize effectively across multiple RFPs and deliver high-quality work against hard deadlines
 A commitment to continuously building skills, adopting new ways of working, and embracing new technology to improve how work gets done
 A “we before me” approach as a trusted, reliable team player who leads with empathy and respect, seeks diverse input, proactively shares information, and contributes to a connected and inclusive culture
 Analytical depth and strong attention to detail in written and numerical content, and the ability to communicate with clarity, transparency, and integrity, escalating risk concerns early
 Fluent written and verbal communication skills in English
 Sound investment knowledge across asset classes and advanced Microsoft Excel and Word
 
 Our benefits 

 To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of benefits including a strong retirement plan, tuition reimbursement, comprehensive healthcare, support for working parents and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about. 
 
 
 Our hybrid work model 
 
 BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.
 
 
Guidance on AI use for candidates 

 At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance  on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.


 About BlackRock 

 At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being.  Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.

 This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive.

 To learn more about BlackRock, please visit Careers.BlackRock.com . We also encourage you to get to know us on LinkedIn , Instagram , YouTube , X , and TikTok .

 BlackRock is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.  We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to age, disability, family status, gender identity, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation and other protected attributes at law.

Position Summary 
 Carlyle seeks to hire a Product Specialist – Associate within Carlyle AlpInvest’s Investor Relations Team. The Associate will work across product lines including Secondary, Co-Investment, NAV Finance, and Primary Investments, supporting efforts in the Institutional channels.

 The Associate will take on meaningful ownership of workstreams, including managing complex investor requests, coordinating diligence processes, contributing to product messaging, and supporting fundraising execution. The role includes regular interaction with limited partners and internal stakeholders, requiring strong analytical, communication, and project management skills. The successful candidate must be able to build expertise in the strategies in which Carlyle AlpInvest operates, manage multiple priorities independently, and perform effectively in a deadline‑driven environment.

 Primary Responsibilities: 
 Key responsibilities include, among others:
 Prepare client update presentations and investment plans, and update marketing and fundraising materials, including due-diligence responses, RFIs, and RFPs
 Support in the day‑to‑day management of investor inquiries and coordination of multi‑stakeholder responses
 Assist with the development of product messaging and value propositions for fundraising initiatives
 Support cross-functional coordination with investment, legal, tax, reporting, operations, and sales teams to respond to investor requests
 Manage portions of the investor due diligence process, including data room preparation, follow‑up coordination, and diligence trackers
 Maintain investor pipelines, diligence trackers, and CRM data to ensure accuracy and timely updates
 Utilize CRM systems and reporting platforms to extract, analyze, and synthesize LP data
 Provide guidance to analysts on materials preparation and workflow organization
 
 Requirements 
 Education & Certificates 
 Bachelor’s degree required with good academic results
   
 Professional Experience 
 2–5 years of relevant experience in investment banking, private equity, management consulting, asset management, international law firms, or comparable blue-chip environments
 Private equity, secondaries, co-investments, or structured finance exposure preferred  
 
 Competencies & Attributes 
 Fluent in English; Japanese language proficiency preferred; additional Asian languages a plus
 Strong ability to interpret quantitative data, financial models, and legal/operational documents
 Excellent computer skills, including ability to learn and become the subject matter expert in the systems used to respond to investor and Senior Product Specialist requests
 Capable of managing complex workstreams with limited supervision
 Team player with ability to work effectively under pressure and manage multiple tasks and changing priorities
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, tailored to professional investor audiences
 Demonstrated initiative, ownership mentality, and ability to work in a fast‑paced environment
 High level of energy and enthusiasm for private equity, investor relations, and client engagement
 Strong organizational skills and detail oriented
 
 Position-specific Technical Requirements 
 Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills required.
 Experience with CRM systems (DealCloud preferred).
 Ability to quickly build proficiency in various reporting platforms and extract actionable insights from LP data.

 When people, ideas, and capital come together, opportunity expands across private markets. At Carlyle, this belief has shaped how we invest for decades, fueling growth for companies and delivering performance for investors.
  
 Visit our website to learn more about our firm and the ways our platform is shaping private markets.

About this role 
 
 
 Role Description ​ 
 The Insight Client Success Team is seeking a Technical Account Manager with a strong financial background to work closely with our Limited Partner (LP) clients. This role will manage strategic client relationships and ensure high-quality service delivery, build strong, trusted client partnerships, advocate for client needs, and ensure consistent execution of Insight Data Services in close collaboration with the broader global Insight organization.​

 3+ years exp in Developing deep expertise in the LP Alternative Asset industry and the Insight platform, partnering with LP clients throughout onboarding and ongoing service delivery.​ 
 Build strong client relationships and lead quarterly data collection campaigns, ensuring high-quality, complete and consistent data while coordinating across Account Management, Product and Onboarding teams.​ 
 Advocate for clients by gathering feedback, driving service improvements, supporting product enhancements and delivering training and enablement.​ 
 Partner across eFront, Aladdin and BlackRock to support client outcomes and product integration.​ 
 As a Technical Account Manager , collaborate closely with your team and global colleagues, share knowledge and best practices, and contribute to consistent execution across the global Insight organization.​ 
 ​ 
 Experience Required: ​ 
 Degree in Finance, Economics, Technology, or a related field. ​ 
 Strong interest in financial markets; knowledge of alternative assets is an advantage. ​ 
 Proven ability to operate independently in a fast-paced, client-focused environment and effectively manage competing priorities. ​ 
 Excellent communication, presentation and stakeholder management skills. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel. ​ 
 Experience in a financial technology firm, client relationship management, account management, or investment data operations is preferred. ​ 
 Experience mentoring or supporting colleagues is an advantage. ​ 
 Ability to collaborate across teams and contribute to initiatives across a global organization.​ 
 
 
 Our benefits 

 To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of benefits including a strong retirement plan, tuition reimbursement, comprehensive healthcare, support for working parents and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about. 
 
 
 Our hybrid work model 
 
 BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.
 
 
Guidance on AI use for candidates 

 At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance  on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.


 About BlackRock 

 At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being.  Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.

 This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive.

 To learn more about BlackRock, please visit Careers.BlackRock.com . We also encourage you to get to know us on LinkedIn , Instagram , YouTube , X , and TikTok .

 BlackRock is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.  We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to age, disability, family status, gender identity, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation and other protected attributes at law.

About Invesco 
 
 As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco. 
 
 What's in it for you? 
 
 Our people are at the very core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our comprehensive compensation and benefit offerings including:  
 Generous annual leave plus f lexible paid time off 

 Hybrid work schedule  

 Learning and development programs 

 Health & wellbeing benefits  

 Parental Leave benefits  

 Employee stock purchase plan (if applicable in your region) 

 
 Job Description 
 
 We are seeking a highly motivated Analyst to join the Asia Pacific Portfolio Management team. The role will primarily support the management of separate account mandates across the region, working closely with portfolio managers, acquisitions teams, asset managers, finance, research and client-facing teams.

 The position provides broad exposure across the investment lifecycle, including portfolio management, investor reporting, fundraising support, investment analysis and business plan monitoring. The successful candidate will support senior team members in delivering accurate analysis, clear client communications and effective coordination across regional and global stakeholders.

 Key Responsibilities
 
 Portfolio Management & Investor Reporting 
 Support the day-to-day management and oversight of separate account mandates across Asia Pacific.
 Prepare quarterly, monthly and ad hoc investor reports, portfolio reviews, presentations and supporting analysis.
 Monitor portfolio performance and maintain portfolio analytics, benchmarks, business plan data and key performance indicators.
 Assist with portfolio construction analysis, capital deployment tracking, cash flow forecasting and liquidity monitoring.
 Coordinate responses to information requests from investors, consultants and internal stakeholders.
 
 Fundraising & Client Support 
 Assist with fundraising and capital-raising initiatives for existing and prospective separate account clients.
 Prepare and update pitch books, due diligence questionnaires, consultant surveys, client presentations and other marketing materials.
 Coordinate investor meetings, roadshows and follow-up materials.
 Support onboarding activities for new investors and mandates, working with legal, compliance, finance and other relevant teams.
 
Investments & Acquisitions Support 
 Work with regional acquisitions teams to evaluate potential investment opportunities for separate account mandates.
 Review underwriting assumptions and assist with financial modelling, sensitivity analysis and investment return analysis.
 Support the preparation of investment committee papers and other transaction approval materials.
 Support financing and hedging analysis and execution, and monitor interest-rate and FX market movements.
 Assist with transaction execution and coordination across internal teams, external advisers and counterparties.
 
 Asset Management & Portfolio Monitoring 
 Work closely with regional asset management teams to monitor asset performance and execution of approved business plans.
 Track key operating initiatives, leasing, development progress, capital expenditure and other asset-level priorities.
 Assist with valuation reviews, asset business plan updates and portfolio-level analysis.
 Prepare materials and analysis for portfolio reviews, asset management meetings and investment committees.
 
 Strategic Projects & Business Management 
 Assist with regional strategic initiatives, portfolio analytics, data management and process improvement projects.
 Coordinate with regional and global teams on reporting, governance and operational requirements.
 Provide analysis and execution support for ad hoc projects led by senior members of the Portfolio Management team.
 
 Qualifications 

 Education 
 Bachelor's degree in real estate, finance, economics, accounting, business or a related discipline.
 Strong academic record.
 
 Experience 
 Approximately 1-3 years of relevant experience in real estate, investment management, private equity, investment banking, consulting, valuation, accounting or a related field.
 Exposure to real estate investing, portfolio management, financial analysis or institutional client reporting would be advantageous.
 Outstanding graduates with relevant internship experience may also be considered.
 
 Skills & Competencies 
 Strong quantitative, analytical and financial modelling skills.
 Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.
 High attention to detail and the ability to work accurately with financial and portfolio data.
 Clear written and verbal communication skills in English; proficiency in an additional Asian language would be advantageous.
 Ability to manage multiple workstreams, prioritize effectively and deliver high-quality work within deadlines.
 Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate across functions, seniority levels and cultures.
 Genuine interest in real estate investing, portfolio management and institutional asset management.
 
 Personal Attributes 
 Highly motivated, intellectually curious and eager to learn.
 Proactive and self-driven, with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.
 Commercially minded, with sound problem-solving capabilities.
 Collaborative and team-oriented.
 Professional, adaptable and comfortable working in a fast-paced, cross-cultural environment.
 
 How to Apply: 
 Apply for the role directly here or at  Invesco Careers :  Careers at Invesco | APAC .
 
 ​ To know more about us: 
 About Invesco:  https://www.invesco.com/corporate/en/home.html 
 About our Culture:  https://www.invesco.com/corporate/en/about-us/our-culture.html 
 About our CR program:  https://www.invesco.com/corporate/en/our-commitments/corporate-responsibility.html

Yes

At Invesco, our workplace model supports our culture and meets the needs of our clients while providing flexibility our employees value. As a full-time employee, compliance with the workplace policy means working with your direct manager to create a schedule where you will work in your designated office at least four days a week, with one day working outside an Invesco office.

Job Description 
 Who we are 
  
 Aberdeen Investments is part of Aberdeen Group plc, one of the UK’s leading Wealth & Investments groups.
  
 Strengthening talent and culture is one of our strategic priorities. We strive to make Aberdeen a great place to work so that we can attract and retain the industry’s best talent.
  
 Our people put our stakeholders at the heart of everything they do by helping us to make a positive difference to the lives of our clients, customers, colleagues, shareholders and society.
  
 We are repositioning our specialist asset management business to meet client demand and are committed to providing excellent client service, supported by leading technology and talent.
  
 As a global business, Aberdeen consists of three divisions: Investments, Adviser, and interactive investor (ii). Each division is dedicated to meeting and adapting to our clients' evolving needs.
  
 Our Asia Pacific Investments business has a large, dedicated and highly experienced investment team which has been investing across the region since 1985, and manages all our Asian products, including regional, country, smaller companies, and sustainable investing propositions.
  
 The team has a strong regional footprint with offices in Singapore, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Seoul, and Sydney. This breadth gives us close proximity to the companies we own and the markets we invest in. Our APAC operations have been based in Singapore since 1992. We invest in Asian companies to grow with them and to help them to become better investors 

Role Purpose 
 Based in Hong Kong, this role provides dedicated support to Aberdeen's Wholesale and Institutional businesses across Greater China, including Hong Kong, China and Taiwan. The position plays a critical role in enabling business growth through sales support, client servicing, consultant engagement and fund research relationship management.

 The successful candidate will work closely with sales, investment specialists, product, marketing and client service teams to support distribution efforts, enhance operational efficiency and strengthen Aberdeen's relationships with key fund research houses and consultants, including Morningstar. 

 This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the continued growth of Aberdeen's Greater China franchise while gaining broad exposure across wholesale, institutional and strategic distribution channels. 

 Requirements 
 Minimum 2 years' experience within financial services, preferably asset management
 Strong interest in financial markets, investment funds and asset allocation solutions
 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills in English and Chinese (Cantonese and Mandarin preferred)
 Experience with Salesforce or other CRM systems preferred
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Sales Support (Wholesale & Institutional) 
 Provide dedicated support to the Wholesale and Institutional sales teams across Greater China.
 Coordinate the preparation of client presentations, investment proposals, due diligence questionnaires (DDQs), RFPs, RFIs and other client materials.
 Support pre-meeting preparation, including gathering market intelligence, portfolio information and customised presentation content.
 Coordinate post-meeting follow-up actions, client requests and information delivery.
 Assist in developing client-facing messaging, sales materials and campaign content while ensuring compliance approvals are obtained.
 Liaise with investment specialists, product teams and subject matter experts to support client enquiries and business development initiatives.
 Support distributor onboarding, institutional mandates and ongoing client servicing activities.
 Ensure accurate maintenance of client and prospect information within Salesforce.
 Support local client events, webinars, roadshows and marketing initiatives across the region.
 Generate sales reports, pipeline analysis and business intelligence to support management decision-making.

 Fund Research & Consultant Relations
 Coordinate fund reviews, analyst meetings and information requests with research providers and consultants.
 Maintain strong working relationships with research analysts, consultants and ratings agencies.
 Coordinate consultant database updates, due diligence submissions and ongoing review processes.
 Partner with investment, product and sales teams to ensure consultants and research providers receive timely and accurate fund information.
 Monitor consultant feedback, fund ratings and research commentary, providing insights to support product positioning and distribution strategies.

 Regional & Strategic Projects 
 Collaborate with broader APAC sales support teams to share best practices and drive operational efficiencies.
 Provide backup support to regional sales support functions as required.
 Participate in strategic projects that support wholesale and institutional business growth across Greater China and APAC.
 Support initiatives related to new fund launches, platform approvals, consultant reviews and distribution opportunities.

Fund or Department Description 
 Carlyle AlpInvest is a leading global private equity investor with over USD 102 billion of assets under management as per September 30, 2025. Approximately 75% of these funds are invested in private equity funds globally, including primary and secondary transactions, with the remainder invested directly in companies as a co-investor in Europe, North America and Asia. The company has approximately 270 employees based primarily in Amsterdam, New York, Hong Kong, London, Singapore and Tokyo. Carlyle AlpInvest is part of The Carlyle Group.
 
 Position Summary 
 Carlyle AlpInvest seeks to hire an Analyst with a focus on primary fund investments with also exposure to secondary and co-investment activities. The Analyst is a two-year program (with optional 6 months extension). Located in our Hong Kong office and reporting to Partner of AlpInvest Primary Investments, the Analyst is expected to play a key role in providing support in investment functions including financial modeling, valuation, analysis of private equity investments, preparation of investment recommendations, post-investment portfolio monitoring, as well as various ad hoc reports and projects as needed.
 
 Primary Responsibilities 
 Applying critical thinking and judgement in the review of PE investment opportunities in funds, to a lesser degree, co and secondaries investment in the region
 Constructing detailed financial models, performance due diligence on fund investment opportunities
 Maintaining database, allocation files
 Monitoring of on-going fund investments, conducting reviews, understanding of portfolio company performance
 Developing relationships with GPs, building personal network
 Preparing periodic investor updates and conducting analyses and support work in developing relationships LP base and fundraising activities
 Support the senior members of in the execution of transactions
 
 Requirements 
 Education & Certificates 
 Bachelor’s Degree in a business-related discipline (accounting, economics, etc.), with good results
 
 Professional Experience 
 Minimum of 2 years of relevant work experience at an investment bank, private equity firm, management consulting or similar setting, with exposure of a wide range of transactions, valuation work and due diligence assignments
 
 Competencies & Attributes 
 Excellent written and spoken English is required
 Knowledge of a second Asian language is considered an advantage
 Proficiency in Excel, Word & PowerPoint, and savvy with latest AI technology
 Strong research and analytical skills as well as superior interpersonal communication and presentation skills
 Familiarity with financial modeling, valuation methodologies and accounting principles
 Ability to communicate confidently and effectively with individuals at all levels of the organization, including senior management
 
 
 Due to the high volume of candidates, please be advised that only candidates selected to interview will be contacted by The Carlyle Group.
 
 ​
 ​
 ​

 Who We Are 

 When people, ideas, and capital come together, opportunity expands across private markets. At Carlyle, this belief has shaped how we invest for decades, fueling growth for companies and delivering performance for investors.
  
 Visit our website to learn more about our firm and the ways our platform is shaping private markets.

The Client Portfolio Analyst (“CPA”) is responsible for completing a variety of analyses and creating client portfolio reports on a regular basis. This position works within the designated Client Portfolio Managers (“CPM”) assisting any of their data and reporting needs. Analysis and content developed by the CPA supports the firm’s efforts to provide outstanding client service as well as to gather and retain assets. The CPA must continuously grow and adapt to changing demands and a wide range of requests for support as markets, strategy lifecycles and performance cycles change. The CPA must excel at working independently while collaborating with many groups across the organization.

 Support Fixed Income CPMs and portfolio managers in response to internal distribution and client inquiries including from prospects, clients, and consultants.
 Reviews, analyzes and interprets attribution and positioning data and creates custom analyses and reports tailored to specific strategies and clients.

 Compiles analysis or data points for client meetings as requested by the CPM.  This may comprise writing specific holding descriptions or more detailed information on portfolio positioning.
 Work closely with CPMs in the content creation process including custom presentations, exhibits and analysis (e.g. sales kits, market outlook slides, new product collateral, etc.) used by CPMs, PMs and other stakeholders (sales, product, marketing teams).
 Work closely with CPMs on relevant ad-hoc projects and developing the ability to work independently and lead such projects overtime.
 Strives to improve investment knowledge (focus on macro and fixed income themes) by conducting research, attending internal investment team calls, reading internal and external research reports.
 Fosters and develops relationships with other departments such as internal/external sales, marketing, performance analytics, product, and client services.
 Key functional back-up of CPMs on all client servicing/reporting activities
 Develops and maintains knowledge on markets, portfolio holdings, portfolio manager thinking and positioning, benchmarks, and peers.
 
 Required Qualifications: 

 Bachelor’s degree in Economics, Finance or a related field
 1-3 years of related investment work experience
 Investment knowledge within Fixed Income asset class preferred
 Progress toward CFA/CAIA accreditations preferred
 Outstanding analytical skills, both quantitative and qualitative
 Able to prioritize work and meet deadlines
 Self-motivated, enthusiastic, responsible, organized, with excellent attention to detail
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with experience in communicating investment matters.  Native/strong proficiency in written and verbal Chinese (Cantonese and Mandarin) preferred
 Excellent computer skills including AI (Co-pilot) and Microsoft Office skills (Excel, Word, PowerPoint)
 Capable of building and maintaining strong relationships with CPMs, Portfolio Managers, and other investment and business team colleagues

About the Opportunity 
Job Type: Fixed Term Contractor 
 
Contract duration : 6 months. 
 
Application Deadline: 21 November 2026 
 
 Title      Marketing Specialist (6-month contract)
 Department      Hong Kong Marketing
 Location          Hong Kong
 Reports To       Chief Marketing Officer, APAC
 Level                4
   
   
 We’re proud to have been helping our clients build better financial futures for over 50 years. How have we achieved this? By working together - and supporting each other - all over the world. So, join our Hong Kong Marketing team and feel like you’re part of something bigger.
   
 About your team 
  
 Join a dynamic and collaborative marketing team supporting Hong Kong Wholesale, Private Banking and Institutional businesses. You'll gain hands-on exposure to high-profile client events, integrated marketing campaigns, thought leadership initiatives and strategic projects while working closely with a diverse group of business partners across the firm.
  
 About your role 
   
 We are seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Marketing Specialist to join our Hong Kong Marketing team to support campaigns and business needs in Hong Kong.
  
 This role offers a unique opportunity to gain broad exposure to the asset management industry and work across multiple client segments, including Hong Kong Wholesale, Private Bank and Institutional businesses. The successful candidate will support a wide range of marketing activities, from client events and campaigns to reporting, communications and day-to-day marketing operations.
  
 This is an ideal opportunity for an early-career marketing professional looking to develop hands-on experience in a fast-paced, global financial services environment.
  
 Key responsibilities 
 Execute marketing campaigns and client engagement initiatives supporting Hong Kong Wholesale, Private Banking and Institutional client segments.
 Support the planning and delivery of client events, conferences, seminars, webinars and sponsorship activities across a range of investment capabilities and business priorities including Digital Assets, Private Assets, and ETFs.
 Manage end-to-end event logistics, including invitations, RSVP management, venue coordination, marketing materials and on-site support.
 Liaise with internal stakeholders, vendors and external partners to ensure timely and compliant execution of marketing activities.
 Support the maintenance of marketing materials and digital content to support client engagement and business objectives.
 Prepare marketing reports, track budgets and assist with campaign and event performance analysis.
 Manage day-to-day marketing administration, including purchase orders, invoicing, vendor management and budget reconciliation.
 Provide general project and administrative support to the Hong Kong Marketing team.
  
   
 About you 
  
 Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, Finance or a related discipline.
 1-3 years of marketing, communications, events or related experience preferred.
 Fresh graduates with strong internship experience are also encouraged to apply.
 Strong organizational and project management skills with excellent attention to detail.
 Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively under tight deadlines.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
 Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly PowerPoint and Excel.
 Experience in financial services, asset management or wealth management is an advantage, but not essential.
  

 Feel rewarded 
 For starters, we’ll offer you a comprehensive benefits package. We’ll value your wellbeing and support your development. And we’ll be as flexible as we can about where and when you work – finding a balance that works for all of us. It’s all part of our commitment to making you feel motivated by the work you do and happy to be part of our team.
  
 
 For more about our work, our approach to dynamic working and how you could build your future here, visit careers.fidelityinternational.com.

description:
Join Hamilton Lane, a global leader in private markets, as we scale to meet the demands of our growing client base. Here, you’ll work with ambitious, high‑performing teams built on integrity, candor and collaboration, backed by our market-leading data and technology. We invest heavily in our people and our partners, giving you the platform to enrich lives, safeguard futures and grow your career.  
  
What We Do  
As one of the largest private markets investment firms globally, we provide innovative solutions to institutional and private wealth investors around the world, specializing in flexibility and full-spectrum access. We currently employ approximately 800 professionals operating in offices throughout North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and the Middle East, and have $1.0 trillion in assets under management and supervision, composed of $146.1 billion in discretionary assets and $871.5 billion in non-discretionary assets, as of December 31, 2025.
 
  
 The Opportunity: 
 The Associate, Secondaries will be responsible for evaluating secondary investments in private equity funds and companies on a global basis with a focus on Asia opportunities. Secondary professionals develop skills relevant to both fund and direct private equity investing, while participating in one of the fastest-growing segments of the private markets industry. Involvement in private equity direct and co-investments is also expected for this role.
  
 Your responsibilities will be to: 
 Assume a lead role in the modelling and analysis of private equity secondary transactions and direct equity transactions.
 Prepare investment memoranda for the Firm’s Investment Committee
 Analyze private equity companies and funds using leveraged buyout models, construct comparable company analyses and develop multiple projection scenarios through company and industry research
 Perform due diligence calls and participate in due diligence meetings with general partners
 Monitor existing investments in the firm’s secondary and direct equity portfolios and assist in preparation of client marketing materials
 Oversight of secondary Analysts in conjunction with the responsibilities listed above
 Support senior team members in originating new investment opportunities and begin networking to develop relationships internally with colleagues and externally with GPs, LPs, intermediaries, etc.
  
 Your background will include: 
 A minimum of 2 years’ experience within the following segments of the financial industry: private equity, investment banking, corporate M&A, capital markets or valuation services
 Prior private equity secondary or direct equity related investment experience is a positive, but not required.
 Demonstrated interest in learning and responsibly applying approved AI tools to support research, analysis, and workflow improvement.
 Experience performing complex financial analysis, modelling, and company valuations
 Ability to conduct industry research, articulate opinions and write clear and concise memoranda on investment opportunities
 Strong written and oral communication and interpersonal skills
 Strong interest and commitment to private equity investing
 Strong work ethic and professional demeanour
 Willingness to be flexible with working hours to work beyond core hours when needed, recognizing this is a fast paced and global organization.
 A team-oriented approach and an ability to interact productively within a diverse company environment
   Outstanding academic record
  
 Travel Requirements: 
  
 Travel up to 10% of time
 
 
 Benefits 
 At Hamilton Lane, our benefits philosophy is simple: to provide our employees with a competitive suite of benefits and services to help navigate through the complexities and challenges of working, living, raising a family, and eventually retiring. 
 To do this, Hamilton Lane offers the following benefits: 
 
 Enhancing Your Physical and Emotional Health  
 Employees have access to healthcare coverage, mental health resources, health & fitness reimbursement program, and Wellness Rewards Program. 
 
 Developing Your Career 
 Tuition and certification reimbursement programs are available, along with continual education and development trainings for you to grow with Hamilton Lane. 
 
 Supporting Your Family & Community 
 For our communities, Hamilton Lane provides paid time off to volunteer and compensates for referring qualified candidates that join our team.  
 For growing family, we offer an adoption reimbursement program, paid time off for new parents and newlyweds, and provide travel support for nursing parents.   
 
 Safeguarding Your Financial Wellbeing 
 Hamilton Lane contributes to retirement programs and offers an employee stock purchasing plan. 
 
 
 
 
 Hamilton Lane is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to their race, religion, ancestry, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, marital status, domestic partner status, or medical condition. As a registered investment adviser, employees of Hamilton Lane may be subject to certain limitations on political contribution and personal investment activities.
 
 Hamilton Lane is not accepting unsolicited assistance from search firms for this employment opportunity. Please, no phone calls or emails. All resumes submitted by search firms to any employee at Hamilton Lane via-email, the Internet or in any form and/or method without a valid written search agreement in place for this position will be deemed the sole property of Hamilton Lane. No fee shall be paid in the event the candidate is hired by Hamilton Lane as a result of the referral or through other means.

Position Responsibilities: 

 Prepare and maintain regular sales and production reports, ensuring accuracy, completeness and timely delivery to management and frontline Sales.
 Perform detailed data validation, reconciliation and analysis to support sales performance monitoring and management reporting.
 Support the implementation and administration of sales campaigns and incentive programs, including production and eligibility validation, incentive calculation, result tracking and payout preparation.
 Develop and maintain Excel-based reports, trackers and calculation tools to support sales monitoring, campaign management and incentive administration.
 Analyze sales and production data to identify trends, performance gaps and areas requiring follow-up, and provide relevant information to support business and sales initiatives.
 Perform quality checks and reconciliation to ensure the accuracy of sales reports, campaign results and incentive calculations.
 Support sales administration activities, including validation and processing of forms, records and other sales-related documentation.
 Maintain accurate records and coordinate with frontline Sales and relevant internal stakeholders on outstanding, incomplete or exceptional cases.
 Support management and frontline Sales with ad-hoc data analysis, reporting and information requests.
 Work closely with internal stakeholders to enhance reporting, validation and administrative processes and improve operational efficiency.
 Support other distribution initiatives and ad-hoc assignments as required.
 
 Required Qualifications: 

 University degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Statistics, Data Analytics or a related discipline.
 At least 2 years of relevant experience in sales reporting, sales operations, incentive calculation, campaign management, data analysis or a related field.
 Strong numerical and analytical skills with the ability to work accurately with detailed sales and production data.
 Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including PivotTables, lookup functions, formulas and data reconciliation; experience in handling and analyzing large datasets is preferred.
 Proficient in Microsoft Word and PowerPoint, with the ability to prepare clear reports and presentation materials.
 Knowledge or hands-on experience in Power BI, SQL or other data visualization and analytical tools would be an advantage.
 Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy, particularly in data validation, calculation and reporting.

Job Summary 
  To support the end-to-end delivery of Investor Services by processing investor onboarding and lifecycle activities accurately, in accordance with fund governing documents and internal controls requirements. The role provides timely and responsive service to clients and investors while maintaining complete records and escalating exceptions appropriately.
  
 Job Duties and Responsibilities 
  · Process investor activities accurately and within agreed deadlines, including subscriptions or commitments, capital calls, distributions, redemptions where applicable, transfers and investor detail changes.
 · Review investor instructions and supporting documentation for completeness, authorised signatures, fund eligibility, notice requirements and compliance with fund governing documents and procedures.
  · Set up and maintain investor, commitment and transaction data in the relevant investor servicing systems, ensuring records are complete and accurate.
  · Prepare and issue investor communications and transaction documents, including acknowledgements, capital call notices, distribution notices, contract notes, statements and other periodic reports.
 · Support fund closings and subsequent closings, including the processing of new or increased commitments and coordination of related investor documentation.
  · Maintain investor capital activity records and support the reconciliation of commitments, contributions, distributions and outstanding balances with Fund Accounting and other internal teams.
 · Coordinate investor payment activities in line with established payment controls, authorised bank instructions and internal approval requirements.
 · Respond promptly and professionally to investor and client enquiries, escalating exceptions, missing information and time-sensitive matters to the supervisor or manager.
 · Work closely with Fund Accounting, AML/KYC, Tax, Client Service, Cash and other operational teams to meet client deliverables and resolve breaks or exceptions.
  · Perform self-review and quality checks to ensure transactions, correspondence, reports and attachments are accurate before submission for review or release.
  · Maintain complete records and audit trails in accordance with internal policies, procedures, information classification requirements and applicable regulations.
  · Assist with new fund launches, client onboarding, system setup, procedure documentation, testing and change initiatives.
 · Identify recurring issues and contribute to process improvements, standardisation and risk reduction within the Investor Services team.
 · Support team knowledge sharing, cross-training and operational coverage as required.
  
 Knowledge, Skills & Experience Required 
 · Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  · Relevant fund administration or transfer agency experience, preferably supporting hedge, private equity, private credit, real assets or other closed-ended alternative funds.
 · Working knowledge of hedge/private equity fund structures and investor lifecycle events, including commitments, capital calls, distributions, transfers and closings.
  · Understanding of investor eligibility, authorised-signatory and payment-control requirements.
  · Strong administrative, organisational and business support skills, with the ability to manage multiple deadlines and work calmly under pressure.
  · Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint; experience with investor servicing or transfer agency systems is an advantage.
  · Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly with clients, investors and internal teams.
 · High level of accuracy, ownership and attention to detail, including the ability to self-review work before submission for approval.
 · Proactive and able to work independently while contributing effectively as part of a team.
  
 Core Competencies 
 Accurate and precise
 Control and risk focused
 Client and investor focused
 Team oriented · Organised and able to prioritise
 Flexible and adaptable
 Proactive and self-reliant
 Strong communication skills

description:
Who we are looking for 
 We are seeking a client-focused support specialist to provide client service and production support for the Fund Connect trading platform. The ideal candidate combines strong operational judgment, technical aptitude, attention to detail, and the ability to coordinate effectively across clients, business partners, and technology teams.

 Why this role is important to us 
 The team is part of State Street Markets (SSM), State Street’s investment research and trading business. Institutional asset owners and managers rely on SSGM for research, trading, securities lending, and innovative portfolio strategies. By combining technology, market expertise, and connectivity across asset classes and global markets, SSGM helps clients enhance and preserve portfolio value.
 Join us if you are ready to make an immediate impact in the capital markets industry while supporting a global, client-focused platform.
  
 What you will be responsible for 
 As a Fund Connect Support Specialist, you will:
 Support the onboarding of new money market clients.
 Support onboarding and fund maintenance for Fund Connect’s ETF offering.
 Assist with onboarding new administrative operators.
 Coordinate data setup and maintenance with the Fund Connect development team.
 Investigate and resolve client inquiries and production issues.
 Review account balances for completeness and source updated data as needed.
 Build and maintain relationships with portal providers.
 Monitor data, trade, and file-transfer integrations and coordinate issue resolution.
 Provide platform training to operators.
 Participate in testing and training for new features.
 Assist portal operators with maintaining user acceptance testing (UAT) environments, including balance updates and fund information.
 Collect and track testing feedback and enhancement requests.
 Ensure adherence to operational procedures and develop new procedures as needed.
 Participate in periodic service-level agreement (SLA) reviews.
 Design and implement operational controls to mitigate risks associated with new business.
 Participate in the regional production-support schedule, including off-hours coverage as needed.
 Assist with developing and implementing process-monitoring tools, workflow-management tools, and client data-sharing workflows.
 Liaise with fund companies on trading, fund maintenance, and onboarding activities.
 Support direct and non-direct money market trading models for Fund Connect clients.
 Advance strategic initiatives established by GlobalLink and Global Markets.
 Manage holiday calendars and client notifications.
 Review fund information on the platform for completeness and accuracy.
  
   What we value 
 The following capabilities will help you succeed in this role:
 Strong attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
 Ability to build and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
 Excellent interpersonal, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
 Ability to prioritize competing demands and deliver high-quality work in a deadline-driven environment.
 
 Education & Preferred Qualifications 
 Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience in financial services.
 Demonstrated client service experience.
 Strong technical aptitude and proficiency with a broad range of applications, including Microsoft Office, Grafana, Freshdesk, Microsoft Teams, and other virtual collaboration tools.
 Ability to understand and navigate a complex global organization.
 Comfort working in a remote environment, including participating in virtual training and providing and receiving feedback.
 Fluency in English is required; proficiency in additional languages (Japanese and/or Korean) is a plus.
 Five or more years of relevant financial services experience, including at least three years in operations or client service.
 Working knowledge of the financial services industry and related financial instruments.
 
 About State Street 

 Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.

 We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.

 As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we consider all qualified applicants for all positions without regard to race, creed, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, age, disability, genetic information, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, citizenship, marital status, domestic partnership or civil union status, familial status, military and veteran status, and other characteristics protected by applicable law.
